13: MATRYÓNA [ in a low voice ] Dig a hole; then we'll bring it out and get it out of the way in a trice! There, she's calling again. Now then, get in, and I'll go.
12: NIKÍTA. What am I to get done?
11: MATRYÓNA. Not manage to do it in one's own house? We'll manage it so that no one will have an inkling. Only do as I tell you. We women can't do it without a man. There, take the spade, and get it done there,—I'll hold the light.
10: NIKÍTA. And supposing it's found out?
8: MATRYÓNA. A living soul indeed! Why, it's more dead than alive. And what's one to do with it? Go and take it to the Foundlings'—it will die just the same, and the rumour will get about, and people will talk, and the girl be left on our hands.
7: MATRYÓNA. What? You're not thinking of backing out, are you? Now it's come to this, and you back out! NIKÍTA. Think what a thing it would be! It's a living soul.
6: NIKÍTA. You'll be getting me into a mess!
5: NIKÍTA. What do you mean to do? MATRYÓNA. We know what to do. You do your share!
3: MATRYÓNA. Why are you sitting there like a hen on a perch? What did your wife tell you to do? You just get things ready!
2: Enter Matryóna with a lantern and spade, panting.
1: ANÍSYA [ raising her arm as if to strike ] I'll give it you! You be off and don't let me catch sight of you! [ Nan runs into hut. To Nikíta ] Do as you're told, or else mind! [ Exit ].
0: NAN. Mammy dear, truly, I swear …
